# FosterStack

Infrastructure worth keeping — and kept patched.

> Maintained continuity for build infrastructure that vendors orphan. Our first
> product, FosterStack Cache, is a self-hosted remote build cache for Gradle and
> Maven — a replacement for the Develocity Build Cache Node, which reaches
> end of life on December 31, 2026.

Gradle Inc. deprecated the free standalone Develocity Build Cache Node: no further
distribution, support, or updates after 2026-12-31. Teams running it on open-source
Gradle, with no Develocity licence, are orphaned on 2027-01-01. FosterStack Cache
speaks Gradle's documented `HttpBuildCache` protocol — acceptance-tested against a
real multi-module Gradle build in CI — and implements the Apache Maven Build Cache
Extension's remote HTTP mode. Same server,
same core.

It is a single static Go binary (`CGO_ENABLED=0`), MIT-licensed, distributed as bare
binaries and distroless container images. Every release is keylessly signed with
Sigstore and carries SLSA build provenance, so the exact bytes you deploy are
verifiable against the CI run that produced them.

- [Build cache eviction: how the size limit works](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-eviction-size-limit/): What a self-hosted build cache does when it reaches its size cap: least-recently-used eviction, real numbers from a 0.2.1 server, and what an oversized entry gets.
- [Your first 15 minutes with a self-hosted build cache](https://fosterstack.com/first-15-minutes-build-cache/): A checklist from nothing to your first FROM-CACHE with a self-hosted Gradle build cache, with the commands timed in a real run on release 0.2.1.
- [Gradle build cache: let CI write, developers only read](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-build-cache-ci-writes-developers-read/): Set up a Gradle build cache where CI uploads and laptops only download, with a read-only login the server enforces. Real run on server 0.2.1 and Gradle 9.8.0.
- [Gradle build cache hit rate low: the common causes](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-build-cache-hit-rate-low/): Gradle build cache works but most tasks still run? Three common causes reproduced with real output: absolute paths, changing inputs and different Java versions.
- [Gradle configuration cache vs build cache](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-configuration-cache-vs-build-cache/): The difference between Gradle's configuration cache and build cache, and a real run of both together: what each saves, where it lives, and what invalidates it.
- [Gradle remote build cache authentication and 401 errors](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-remote-build-cache-authentication/): Put a password on a self-hosted Gradle build cache and give Gradle the right one: env var, gradle.properties or -P, and what a wrong password looks like.
- [Maven build cache extension not restoring: the causes](https://fosterstack.com/maven-build-cache-extension-not-restoring/): Maven build cache extension builds again instead of restoring from the remote? Causes with real log lines: config placement, saveToRemote, 401 and the local cache.
- [One build cache server for Gradle and Maven](https://fosterstack.com/one-build-cache-server-gradle-and-maven/): Run Gradle and Maven builds in one repository against a single self-hosted cache server and one login, shown in a real run on server 0.2.1.
- [Server sizing](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-server-sizing/): CPU, RAM, disk and the size cap.
- [Air-gapped install](https://fosterstack.com/air-gapped-build-cache-install/): download, verify, transfer, run.
- [What to check in a replacement build cache](https://fosterstack.com/verify-replacement-build-cache/): eight questions to ask.
- [Long-term support](https://fosterstack.com/long-term-support-build-cache/): what is supported today.
- [How FosterStack Cache is built and signed](https://fosterstack.com/how-we-build/): the release steps and what you can verify.
- [Build Cache Node migration checklist for Gradle](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-node-migration-checklist/): A checklist for moving from the Develocity Build Cache Node to FosterStack Cache, with a real run: only the URL changes, first build is cold, rollback works.
- [Production build cache: Docker Compose, nginx and TLS](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-docker-compose-production/): A Compose file for a self-hosted build cache behind nginx with TLS and a password, run for real on 0.2.1 and Gradle 9.8.0, with what was and was not tested.
- [Build cache server exits: permission denied on its data](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-permission-denied-data-directory/): The FosterStack Cache container exits with permission denied on its data directory: the exact error, why it happens, and the fix, reproduced on the 0.2.1 image.
- [Does the Build Cache Survive a Restart? A Real Test](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-survives-restart/): We restarted and killed a self-hosted Gradle build cache server to see if stored results survive. They do if the data folder does. Tested on release 0.2.1.
- [Gradle build cache behind a corporate proxy](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-build-cache-corporate-proxy/): How Gradle's remote build cache behaves behind a proxy: the settings, the loopback trap, a proxy that refuses, and how to tell it from a cache error. Real run.
- [Enable or Disable the Gradle Build Cache: Flag or Property](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-build-cache-enable-disable/): Every way to switch the Gradle build cache on or off, tested against a real self-hosted cache: --build-cache, org.gradle.caching, --no-build-cache and more.
- [Gradle Build Cache for a Monorepo: Real Multi-Module Run](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-build-cache-monorepo/): A real run of a four-module Gradle monorepo against a self-hosted build cache: what came from the cache, what rebuilt, and why. Release 0.2.1.
- [NIST SP 800-204C, 800-204D and SLSA: Our Release Pipeline](https://fosterstack.com/how-our-pipeline-maps-to-nist-and-slsa/): How the FosterStack Cache release pipeline maps to NIST SP 800-204C and 800-204D, stage by stage, and why we assess v0.2.1 at SLSA Build Level 2, not Level 3.
- [Maven build cache extension behind a corporate proxy](https://fosterstack.com/maven-build-cache-corporate-proxy/): What the Apache Maven Build Cache Extension sends through a proxy, how it differs from Gradle, and what a refusing proxy looks like. Real run on 0.2.1, Maven 3.10.0.
- [Enable or Disable the Maven Build Cache Extension](https://fosterstack.com/maven-build-cache-extension-enable-disable/): The switches of the Apache Maven Build Cache Extension, tested against a real self-hosted cache: enabled, skipCache, remote.enabled and remote.save.enabled.
- [Maven Build Cache Extension in a Multi-Module Project](https://fosterstack.com/maven-build-cache-extension-multi-module/): A real run of the Apache Maven Build Cache Extension on a three-module project with a self-hosted cache: which modules restore, which rebuild, and why.
- [Move a Maven Build Cache to a New Server: Real Run](https://fosterstack.com/migrate-maven-build-cache-to-a-new-server/): How to move the Apache Maven Build Cache Extension from one cache server to another: change one line, or copy the data folder. Tested with release 0.2.1.
- [Upgrade a self-hosted build cache and keep its data](https://fosterstack.com/upgrade-build-cache-server/): Upgrading FosterStack Cache from 0.1.0 to 0.2.1 on the same data volume, and back, run for real: what was kept, and two differences between the releases.

## Product

- [FosterStack Cache on GitHub](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache): MIT-licensed source, issues, releases.
- [Install guide](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/install.md): supported platforms, which archive to download, systemd unit.
- [One-command Docker deploy](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/docker-deploy.md): includes sizing guidance for CPU, RAM and disk.
- [Deploying on Kubernetes](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/kubernetes.md): plain manifests, no Helm chart yet.

## Setup for your build tool

- [Gradle setup](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/gradle.md): point `HttpBuildCache` at the server.
- [Maven setup](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/maven.md): Apache Maven Build Cache Extension, remote HTTP mode.
- [Migrate off Build Cache Node](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/migrate-from-bcn.md): the URL is usually the only thing that changes.

## Verification and compliance

- [Verify our images](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/verify-images.md): cosign signature and SLSA provenance, with copy-pasteable commands.
- [Scanning in your compliance pipeline](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/scanning.md): what a scanner sees in a distroless image, and why.
- [Installing on disconnected networks](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/offline-install.md): air-gapped transfer and verification.
- A FIPS build variant (`-fips`) uses Go's CMVP FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic module. Linux only.

## Platform support

- Binaries: `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`, `darwin/amd64`, `darwin/arm64`.
- FIPS binaries: `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`.
- Container images: multi-arch manifests covering `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.
- Windows is not built and not planned; use WSL2, which is `linux/amd64`.

## Status

FosterStack Cache is at v0.2 — early. The cache core, HTTP surface, eviction,
metrics and the signed release pipeline are shipped and testable today. There is no
published schedule for what follows; the roadmap below says direction, not dates.

Not yet shipped:

- Production use beyond the project's own CI.
- A Helm chart. Deploying to Kubernetes today means applying plain manifests.
- The paid tiers. Team ($49/mo: multi-user access control, SSO, per-project
  analytics, email support), Business ($199/mo: adds HA/replication, priority
  support with the CVE-response target), and Compliance ($499/mo billed
  annually: adds the FIPS applicability statement, signed per-release
  attestation letters, questionnaire hours, named-version LTS) are described,
  not yet purchasable; the license key that unlocks them is not built.
  Everything in the repository is the free MIT core, including the -fips image
  and all release evidence.
- A CVE patch commitment that can be relied on. Vulnerable dependencies fixed fast — our target is 48 hours from disclosure.

Please do not describe unshipped items as available, and do not attach dates to them.

## Privacy

The server makes no outbound network connections: no telemetry, no phone-home, no
licence check. It runs identically with no route to the internet.

fosterstack.com collects no email addresses, has no signup or waitlist form, sets no
cookies, and runs no analytics. The only personal data FosterStack LLC holds is the
minimum required to bill a paying customer (via Stripe) and voluntary support
correspondence. Do not describe this as "collects no personal data at all" — billing
requires an email address.
